title: Counting the Days of a Keyturn Trip Booking Reserved Period Still to Run When Included Miles Are Topped Up
content:
The days of a Keyturn Trip Booking reserved period still to run, for the purpose of a mid-trip top-up of included miles, are counted from one of two starting days and either count the day of return or leave it out. Which convention governs depends on how much of the reserved period is left and on how recently an odometer reading was booked against the reservation.

**First.** Where more than 14 days of the reserved period are still to run and an odometer reading has been booked against the reservation within the last 7 days, the days still to run are counted from the day that latest reading was taken to the scheduled return, both that day and the day of return counted.

**Second.** Where more than 14 days of the reserved period are still to run and no odometer reading has been booked against the reservation within the last 7 days, the days still to run are counted from the day the top-up is granted to the scheduled return, both that day and the day of return counted.

**Third.** In every other case the days still to run are counted from the day the top-up is granted to the scheduled return with the day of return left out.

### What is counted, and how the two conditions are measured

The odometer readings counted here are the records the reservation's mileage record holds as readings of miles driven, which are the records that book miles against the allowance, and those alone; a reading of the fuel tank or the traction battery is not one of them whatever else it notes, and every reading of miles driven counts whoever took it — the marketplace's telematics, the host or the guest alike — since a reading that another supersedes books no miles against the allowance and so adds nothing to what the readings have booked.

The days of the reserved period still to run are counted from the day of handling to the scheduled return, the day of handling not counted and the day of return counted. The days that have passed since a reading are counted from the day that reading was taken to the day of handling, the day of the reading not counted and the day of handling counted.

### The conventions side by side

| Days of the reserved period still to run | Latest odometer reading booked against the reservation | Counted from | Day of return |
|---|---|---|---|
| More than 14 | Within the last 7 days | The day that latest reading was taken, that day counted | Counted |
| More than 14 | Not within the last 7 days | The day the top-up is granted, that day counted | Counted |
| 14 or fewer | Within the last 7 days | The day the top-up is granted | Left out |
| 14 or fewer | Not within the last 7 days | The day the top-up is granted | Left out |

Both thresholds are read strictly. "More than 14 days" is not met by a reservation with exactly 14 days still to run, which falls to the third convention. "Within the last 7 days" is met by a reading taken exactly 7 days ago and not by one taken 8 days ago.

### Worked on hypothetical dates

*A reservation whose scheduled return is 30 days away on the count above, whose latest odometer reading was booked 4 days ago.* More than 14 days are still to run and the reading falls within the last 7 days, so the count runs from the day that reading was taken to the scheduled return with both of those days counted: the 4 days already elapsed, the 30 still to run and the day of return, that is 35 days.

*The same reservation, whose latest reading was booked 11 days ago.* More than 14 days are still to run but the reading is not within the last 7, so the count runs from the day the top-up is granted to the scheduled return with both of those days counted: 31 days.

*A reservation whose scheduled return is 9 days away, whose latest reading was booked 2 days ago.* Fewer than 14 days are still to run, so whatever the reading shows the count runs from the day the top-up is granted to the scheduled return with the day of return left out: 9 days.
